# OIG: MA organizations overturned nearly all appealed SNF prior-auth denials

- Citation: HHS Office of Inspector General, OEI-09-24-00331, issued 2026-06-08. https://oig.hhs.gov/reports/all/2026/medicare-advantage-organizations-overturned-nearly-all-appealed-prior-authorization-denials-for-skilled-nursing-facility-admission-raising-concerns-about-initial-denials/
- Year: 2026 (data from June 2024)
- Tier: 1 (government)
- Sample / method: prior-auth requests for SNF admission at 19 Medicare Advantage organizations, June 2024; denial and appeal outcomes compared across MAOs and contractors.
- Key findings:
  - 12% of SNF admission requests were denied; the rate varied by MAO from 0.4% to 23%.
  - 18% of denials were appealed; on appeal, MAOs overturned 95% in favor of the enrollee.
  - Nursing home residents seeking a short-term SNF stay were denied at 40%, against 11% for other enrollees.
  - Denials made by the naviHealth contractor: 14% denial rate; 97% overturned on appeal.
  - Three recommendations to CMS (fix initial review breakdowns, assess variation, examine the nursing-home-resident gap). All are open.
- Limits: one month of data; 19 MAOs; doesn't measure the delay or cost a denial causes before it is overturned. Figures come from the summary page, not the full PDF.

## Nursing home residents (full report read 2026-10-04; PDF https://oig.hhs.gov/documents/audit/11694/OEI-09-24-00331.pdf)
- Definition (fn 32): a nursing home episode of at least 101 cumulative days, started before the SNF request (MDS "long-stay").
- Volume (App. D): 1,965 approved and 1,283 denied (39.5%), about 3% of requests; all others 11.5%.
- Denial reasons: not broken down anywhere in the report. No mention of Jimmo, the "improvement standard" or Chapter 8.
- MAOs' explanations (pp.7-8, OIG reporting, not findings): residents "are less likely to meet the admission criteria for daily SNF-level care because they already have some intermittent skilled therapy supports available"; residents may have "a more complex medical history". naviHealth's supplemental guidance told reviewers "to consider the reasons that the enrollee lives in a nursing facility", which "frequently impact a patient's ability to meaningfully participate in daily skilled therapy"; naviHealth denied residents at a higher rate than other reviewers.
- Advocates and industry: place of residence "should not affect" eligibility; custodial care with intermittent therapy "is not a clinically equivalent substitute".
- Residents' appeal and overturn rates: not reported. CMS did not say whether or how it would act on the resident recommendation.
